newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: REGIONAL VOLATILITY WEAKENS PHILIPPINE PESO.
newsitem.headline: REGIONAL VOLATILITY WEAKENS PHILIPPINE PESO.

text.p: The Philippine peso fell to 29.05 to the dollar at close in sympathy with other regional currencies which came under renewed speculative attacks, traders said.
The central bank was quick to intervene in the morning, selling dollars from 28.70 early in the session to as high as 29.15 by late morning.
On Tuesday, the peso closed at 28.66 to the dollar.
"Some banks saw the 29.00 level as a good level to sell," one trader from a foreign bank said. He said foreign banks which were dollar buyers, slowed down after the peso hit 29.10.
The appetite for dollars was heightened after the Indonesian rupiah fell prey to speculation earlier in the day, tumbling to a historic low before the central raised its interest rates.
A total of $62.55 million changed hands in the Philippine Dealing System, with the central bank estimated to have sold $10 to $15 million.
Traders expected the peso to remain soft in the coming days due to the fresh attack on the regional currencies.
Bids from banks ranged from 28.95 to 28.97 at the close of trading.
